{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABd7mY6w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHcvhI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 263, "title": "Run in-page microphone dictation without opening a separate recording window", "body": "## Goal / user decision

Clicking the microphone button beside a supported Web page text field should **start voice dictation in place**, without opening a small extension recording window. Clicking the same button again stops it. The user should remain focused on the original page and input field throughout.

**A visible extension window is not an acceptable normal recording UI.** Chrome's microphone permission prompt may appear when permission is required, but a separate extension window must not be shown just to host recognition. Do not confuse the OS/browser permission prompt with an extension-owned recording window.

## Current behavior and constraints

- `extension/web-voice-content.js` inserts the page mic widget and binds the target field/caret.
- `extension/web-voice-runtime.js` currently executes a `TabSession` inside a small, visible `extension/web-voice-runtime.html` window; it prepares models, requests microphone via `getUserMedia`, runs the graph and closes itself on Stop/Cancel.
- The Web voice coordinator opens/owns that document and routes its extension-only messages; the content script remains in Chrome's isolated world.
- `docs/chrome-extension.md` says the visible runtime was chosen because an offscreen document cannot reliably present a **first-use microphone permission prompt**. That is an implementation consideration, **not** a requirement to show a window for every dictation session.
- Preserve independent concurrent Live/Web sessions introduced by #256 / PR #258. This change must not reintroduce a global inference lock.

## Required UX

1. When the user clicks the page microphone, the **same in-page button** shows Preparing → Recording → Stopping/Idle (or an actionable Error). No extension-owned window/tab/popup should visibly appear during ordinary use.
2. Chrome's native microphone permission request may be shown **only when needed**. After grant, recording proceeds without an extension-owned recording window. On later clicks, where permission is already granted, there should be **no separate visible window at all**.
3. The in-page control remains the primary way to Stop/Cancel. Preserve its visibility/stop access if focus changes or the target scrolls offscreen.
4. Final recognized text is inserted exactly once into the originally bound field; no automatic submit, no wrong-field redirection, no provisional text appended as final.
5. Permission denial, device failure, model/cache error, navigation, target removal, disabling Web microphone, extension reload and cancellation all cleanly end that one session and show a useful error where possible. No orphan microphone capture/Workers.

## Implementation: verify Chrome feasibility, then implement

**Do not assume** that `chrome.offscreen` + `USER_MEDIA` can always display a first-time microphone permission prompt. Before choosing architecture, test the actual supported Chrome permission paths and record findings.

- Investigate a nonvisible **extension-owned runtime** (e.g. an Offscreen Document with the appropriate `offscreen` permission and `USER_MEDIA` reason, if supported), including first grant vs already granted permission, user activation, `getUserMedia`, audio worklets, model workers, CPU/WASM and any GPU-dependent nodes.
- If first-time permission cannot be obtained from a nonvisible context, design a **minimal, explicitly user-initiated one-time permission setup flow** that can obtain consent without a recurring tiny recording window. A browser permission prompt is expected; avoid silently asking for broader permissions or falsely claiming it can be shown without a visible document. Do not open the old recording window for each dictation as a hidden fallback. If a visible setup page is technically unavoidable for first grant, it must be a clear, one-time permission setup, not a recording host, and document the exact Chrome constraint.
- Keep inference out of the host page/content script and MV3 service worker. Use an extension-owned DOM-capable execution context and secure authenticated message routing; never expose models or private transcripts to arbitrary page scripts.
- Reuse the existing graph snapshot, `TabSession`, model preparation, worker pipeline, permissions and content-script target/capability/sequence safeguards. Avoid adding an unrelated new graph runtime or changing the graph schema.
- Scope runtime ownership and cleanup to the correct Web session/document/tab. Support concurrent Live and independent Web sessions; no global Busy admission gate. Offscreen document lifecycle and concurrency must account for Chrome's offscreen-document limits (e.g. a coordinator with multiple independently owned sessions in one offscreen document, or another proven-safe architecture), rather than assuming one offscreen document per tab is always allowed.
- Consider what happens if the browser discards/restarts the MV3 service worker or offscreen context. Maintain reliable Stop, status, cleanup and late-event rejection.
- Preserve current explicit Web microphone opt-in, host permission gating and native microphone permission semantics. Avoid requesting new broad website access merely to remove the window.

## Acceptance criteria / verification

- [ ] Clicking the in-page mic starts dictation without opening a visible extension-owned recording window/tab in the normal already-authorized path.
- [ ] First-time microphone permission works with a clear user-initiated flow. Chrome's native permission prompt is allowed; if a separate setup page is unavoidable, it appears **only for initial setup**, not for ordinary recordings. Document why.
- [ ] Same in-page mic button handles Preparing, Recording, Stop/Cancel and Error without focus theft.
- [ ] Existing target/caret identity, exactly-once final insertion, no auto-submit, stale-message protection and Web OFF/permission revoke behavior are retained.
- [ ] Multiple Web sessions and concurrent Live + Web sessions work without a global runtime lock or shared-worker/track teardown.
- [ ] Model preparation, verified assets, offline processing and graph eligibility remain intact. Genuine resource errors are surfaced per session.
- [ ] Cancellation, rapid repeated clicks, navigation, closing a tab, device end, permission denial/revocation, service worker restart and extension reload do not leak microphone capture or insert late text.
- [ ] Automated Chrome/MV3 tests cover first grant, subsequent granted use, denied grant, visible-window absence, concurrent sessions and cleanup. Real-model smoke where feasible; record tests actually run and limitations. Do not claim to automate native permission UI buttons if not actually tested.
- [ ] Update docs to remove the claim that an always-visible small runtime window is part of the intended Web microphone UX.

## Scope

This is a **functional/UX improvement**, not a cosmetic resize or hiding the existing window behind another window. Do not modify Graph Library layout (#260), X/Twitter rich-text editor insertion or Live's own visible UI.

Related: #247 (original opt-in Web microphone feature), #256 / PR #258 (independent concurrent runtime sessions).
